Theme

Latin word

vel

adverb: with superlatives, and “even” of something one may choose

even (if you like); or (whichever you like)

In this lexicon

  • even

    also used · classical · Quint. 10.7.25: vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus; Cic. Att. 7.10.1: crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit

  • or

    also used · classical · Cato Agr. 88: maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō; Traupman 354

  • vel … vel: either … or

    classical

  • vel potius: rather

    classical

Examples

  • vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus

    let us speak even alone rather than not speak at allQuint. 10.7.25

    In the entry for even

  • tū, quaesō, crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit

    please write to me often, even whatever comes into your headCic. Att. 7.10.1

    In the entry for even

  • maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō; sī natābit, ea muriēs erit

    drop in a dried sprat or an egg; if it floats, that will be brineCato Agr. 88

    In the entry for or
